- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.0) — cap forecast increase at +3% above immediate prior value.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged rebound.
- If forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction to prevent overshoot bias.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
